idiom_name: Module#prepend or SimpleDelegator wrapping, plus view-component composition
implementation_notes: Ruby enhances a component class from the outside with Module#prepend - the module's methods sit ahead of the class's own in the ancestor chain, so behaviour is added without editing or shadowing the class - while SimpleDelegator and Forwardable wrap an object instance and forward unknown calls to the wrapped object, both documented primitives of the core and standard library. Where components are objects that render themselves (view-component style), composition of view objects is the idiomatic form and no wrapper class is needed. The classic wrapper class is still justified when the enhanced object must be a distinct class, for instance when a framework resolves templates or serializers by class name.
code_sketch:
module Instrumented
  def render(...)                        # prepended: runs before the class's own method
    t = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    result = super                       # the wrapped component is unaware
    track(:render, Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t)
    result
  end
end

PricePanel.prepend(Instrumented)          # applied once, at definition
pitfalls: Module#prepend mutates the class's ancestor chain for every instance, present and future: there is no per-call-site enhancement.
SimpleDelegator hides class identity - is_a?/kind_of? and case/=== no longer match the wrapped component - which breaks framework dispatch based on class.
method_missing-based delegation swallows NoMethodError and damages backtraces; implement respond_to_missing? and re-raise errors from the wrapped object.
